relevance_reason: Reports a patient with SHFM6 and a novel homozygous WNT10B in-frame deletion.

findings.statement: Kantaputra et al. (2018) reported an Indian girl with split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM), sparse hair, and interrupted eyebrows. The patient and all family members had normal bone density and were not obese, unlike some patients with WNT10B variants. The authors suggested that sparse hair and interrupted eyebrows may be associated findings of SHFM6.
quotes: We report an Indian girl with split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM), sparse hair, and interrupted eyebrows
The patient and all family members had normal bone density and they were not obese like some of the patients with WNT10B variants.
Sparse hair and interrupted eyebrows may be associated findings of SHFM6.

findings.statement: In an Indian girl with SHFM6, Kantaputra et al. (2018) identified a novel homozygous 3-bp deletion in the WNT10B gene (c.695_697delACA), predicted to cause an in-frame deletion of asparagine-232 (p.Asn232del). Protein modeling suggested that this deletion at a critical position likely severely affects protein structure and function, likely decreasing protein lifetime and preventing binding to its receptors and other ligands.
quotes: who carries a novel homozygous deletion c.695_697delACA in WNT10B. The variant is deduced to cause an in-frame deletion of Asn residue 232 (p.Asn232del).
According to the protein model, this single amino acid deletion at the critical position in the protein structure is likely to severely affect the protein structure and function.
This deletion is likely to lead decreased lifetime and make it unable to bind to its receptors and other ligands.

relevance_reason: Reports a sporadic SHFM patient with a homozygous WNT10B truncating mutation, which supports autosomal recessive SHFM6.

findings.statement: In a patient with sporadic split-hand/foot malformation, Blattner et al. (2010) sequenced WNT10B and found a homozygous 4-bp duplication that results in a premature termination codon. Nine relatives who were heterozygous for the duplication showed no sign of SHFM.
quotes: By examining WNT10B in a patient with sporadic SHFM, we identified a homozygous 4-bp duplication resulting in a premature termination codon. Nine heterozygous relatives show no sign of SHFM.

variants.as_reported: 4-bp duplication resulting in a premature termination codon

findings.statement: Blattner et al. (2010) concluded that sporadic SHFM is not always a dominant trait and may be inherited in an autosomal recessive manner. In that case the recurrence risk is 25% for sibs and very low for the offspring of patients unless there is consanguinity. They recommended testing patients with sporadic SHFM for WNT10B mutations to determine the recurrence risk.
quotes: Obviously, sporadic SHFM may show recessive rather than dominant inheritance resulting in a 25% recurrence risk for sibs instead of a very low-recurrence risk as generally presumed.
It can be concluded that sporadic SHFM is not always a dominant trait. To determine the recurrence risk, patients affected with sporadic SHFM should be tested for mutations in WNT10B.

relevance_reason: The paper reports the consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM, maps the locus to 12q13 and identifies a homozygous WNT10B mutation. This defines SHFM6.

findings.statement: Ugur and Tolun (2008) studied a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive split-hand/foot malformation. Twelve affected members had central reductions of the feet, with or without hand involvement. One more affected member had the mildest phenotype, which was atypical SHFM.
quotes: We studied a large consanguineous kindred afflicted with autosomal recessive SHFM.
Twelve affected members had central feet reductions with or without hand involvement while the remaining one had the mildest phenotype and atypical SHFM.

findings.statement: In a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM, Ugur and Tolun (2008) used homozygosity mapping to identify a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13. The maximum multipoint lod score was 5.47. Linkage to 4 of the 5 known SHFM loci was excluded.
quotes: We identified by homozygosity mapping a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13 with a maximum multipoint lod score of 5.47
We also investigated linkage to the five known SHFM loci. Four of the loci were excluded

findings.statement: Using a candidate gene approach in the consanguineous SHFM kindred, Ugur and Tolun (2008) identified a homozygous missense mutation in WNT10B, p.R332W. It was found in all affected individuals except the atypical case, and also in an asymptomatic female. The authors proposed that either a second locus contributes to manifestation of the SHFM phenotype or a suppressor locus prevented manifestation in the nonpenetrant female.
quotes: by subsequent candidate gene approach a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation (p.R332W) in all affected individuals but the atypical case plus in an asymptomatic female
We propose that either a second locus contributes to the manifestation of SHFM phenotype or a suppressor locus prevented trait manifestation in the non-penetrant female.

findings.statement: In most affected members of the kindred, Ugur and Tolun (2008) detected a rare insertion variant in TP63 (rs34201045). It lies at the alternate promoter used to transcribe the N-terminal-truncated p63 isotype. The authors suggested complex inheritance.
quotes: in TP63 [tumor protein p63 (SHFM4)], the only known gene responsible for SHFM, we detected in most affected subjects a rare insertion variant (rs34201045) at the alternate promoter used for transcription of the N-terminal-truncated p63 isotype

relevance_reason: Abstract-only review/analysis of phenotype patterns across mapped SHFM loci in general; SHFM6 and autosomal recessive ectrodactyly are not specifically mentioned. Provides only context on SHFM heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Elliott and Evans (2006) noted that split-hand/foot malformation is genetically heterogeneous, with at least five loci identified. Using descriptive epidemiology, chi-square and discriminant function analyses, they identified phenotypic patterns associated with the mapped SHFM loci, which they suggested could help with classification and with directing mapping efforts and targeted genetic testing.
quotes: genetic heterogeneity, with at least five loci identified to date, further complicates management of affected patients and their families
Using descriptive epidemiology, Chi square and discriminant function analyses, our laboratory has identified phenotypic patterns associated with the mapped genetic SHFM loci.

relevance_reason: Reports an inbred kindred with nine cases of SHFM and argues for autosomal recessive inheritance, which is the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: Gül and Oktenli (2002) reported 9 individuals with split-hand/split-foot malformation (SHFM) in an inbred kindred. The malformation pattern varied within the family.
quotes: Here we report on nine cases of SHFM in an inbred kindred.
A variable intrafamilial expression of the malformation pattern is apparent.

findings.statement: Gül and Oktenli (2002) noted that most familial SHFM is autosomal dominant. In their inbred kindred with 9 affected members, they discussed autosomal recessive inheritance as well as a two-locus model.
quotes: The majority of the familial cases are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.
Autosomal recessive inheritance and a two-locus model are discussed.

relevance_reason: The title describes a recessive form of ectrodactyly, which is this entry's subject (autosomal recessive split-hand/foot malformation). Only the title is available.

findings.statement: Freire-Maia (1971) described a recessive form of ectrodactyly and discussed what it means for genetic counseling.
quotes: A recessive form of ectrodactyly, and its implications in genetic counseling.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It reports split-foot malformation in two sibs, which is relevant to an entry on recessive split-hand/foot malformation.

findings.statement: Ray (1970) reported split-foot malformation in 2 sibs.
quotes: Another case of split-foot mutation in two sibs.

relevance_reason: The paper reports an extended family in which sisters and half sisters had ectrodactyly, and the authors suggest autosomal recessive inheritance. This bears directly on autosomal recessive split-hand/foot malformation.

findings.statement: Mufti and Wood (1987) described an extended family in which 4 sisters and half sisters had ectrodactyly. Two of the sisters also had agenesis of the tibiae.
quotes: An extended family is described in which four sisters and half sisters presented with ectrodactyly.
Two of the sisters had associated agenesis of the tibiae.

findings.statement: Based on the occurrence of ectrodactyly in sisters and half sisters of an extended family, Mufti and Wood (1987) concluded that autosomal recessive inheritance seemed likely.
quotes: An autosomal recessive gene seems likely to be the mode of inheritance.

relevance_reason: The title describes a familial report of ectrodactyly in sisters and half sisters, which bears on the familial or recessive form of split-hand/foot malformation. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: Hennekam and Lommen (1988) reported ectrodactyly in sisters and half sisters.
quotes: Ectrodactyly in sisters and half sisters.

relevance_reason: Describes a family with split hand/foot malformation in two sibships and raises the possibility of an autosomal recessive form, which is this entry's subject.

findings.statement: Zlotogora and Nubani (1989) described a family in which 4 individuals in 2 sibships had typical split hand/foot malformation.
quotes: A family is described in which four subjects in two sibships had typical split hand/foot malformation.

findings.statement: Zlotogora and Nubani (1989) discussed whether a rare autosomal recessive form of split hand/foot malformation exists. As an alternative, they proposed a two-locus model: a dominant split hand/foot mutation would be controlled by a gene at another locus, and a dominant mutation at that controlling locus would cause nonpenetrance of the split hand/foot mutation.
quotes: The possibility of the existence of a rare autosomal recessive form of the malformation is discussed, as well as a two locus model.

In the two locus model the dominant mutation leading to the split hand/foot malformation is controlled by a gene at another locus. A dominant mutation at the controlling locus leads to non-penetrance of the split hand/foot mutation.

relevance_reason: Reports a consanguineous family with split-hand/foot malformation segregating as an autosomal recessive trait, which is what this entry is about.

findings.statement: Verma et al. (1976) described an intermarried consanguineous family in which split-hand and split-foot deformity occurred in 2 sibships. Both sibships came from first-cousin marriages.
quotes: A intermarried consanguineous family with split-hand and -foot deformity occurring in two sibship is presented.
Both the sibship resulted from marriage between first cousins.

findings.statement: Verma et al. (1976) concluded that their family, together with those reported by Ray (1960) and Freire-Maia (1971), further showed that split-hand and split-foot deformity can be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. Their evidence was the occurrence of the deformity in 2 sibships born to first-cousin parents.
quotes: This report, together with those of Ray (1960) and Freire-Maia (1971), further demonstrates that split-hand and -foot deformity can be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait.
